# Improvement suggestions (not acted on — outside this repair's scope)

These are unrelated observations noticed while repairing lifecycle.py / test_lifecycle.py.
None of them were implemented, per the constraint that implementation changes are limited
to fixing the reported contract mismatch.

1. `status()` has no input validation — any value other than the literal string "native"
   currently falls through to the "external" branch (now "verified"). If new workspace
   kinds are ever introduced, this will silently misclassify them instead of raising.
   Consider an explicit allow-list of owner kinds with a clear error for unknown values.

2. `status()` has no docstring or type hints. A one-line docstring stating the current
   contract (and pointing at requirements.md as the source of truth) would help future
   readers avoid re-introducing a stale assertion like the one just fixed in test_native.

3. There is no test covering an unrecognized/invalid `owner` argument (e.g. `None`, `""`,
   or an unexpected string). Only "native" and "external" are exercised today.

4. requirements.md documents only the current contract, and backlog.md only the previous
   one, with no explicit link between them. A short changelog entry (e.g. "contract for
   native changed from verified -> platform-pending on <date>, see backlog.md") would make
   it easier to tell a genuinely obsolete test assertion from an implementation bug next
   time the contract changes.
